newsitem.title: USA: Calif. reporter who covered abuse cases admits murder.
newsitem.headline: Calif. reporter who covered abuse cases admits murder.

text.p: A radio reporter who police say confessed to kidnapping and murdering a two-year-old boy had covered two assignments related to child molestation on the day he turned himself in, a newspaper said Saturday.

Reporter Steven Diddy's arrest for the mysterious kidnap-murder in February of Matthew Moorby has electrified the central California town of Fresno. But The Fresno Bee newspaper reported that some city residents had doubts about Diddy's story.

Diddy, 26, a reporter with KMPH/KFRE News Radio in Fresno, turned himself in to police Thursday afternoon and police said he confessed to murdering Moorby, whose mysterious disappearance and death have been covered intensely by the local media.
Fresno police said Diddy's confession came as "a total surprise".

But police chief Ed Winchester said Thursday that "based on information Mr. Diddy provided us, we believe he is the suspect." Diddy, booked for investigation of kidnapping and murder, is being held in the local jail after bail was set at more than $1 million.
Police have said the child was not molested and they have not revealed a possible motive for the crime. They said Diddy did not know the Moorby family.

Moorby disappeared from an apartment complex Feb. 6 and his body was found floating in a lake two days later. Moorby's mother, 18-year-old Julie Williams, was asleep when he disappeared. Police launched an intensive investigation without success.

The Fresno Bee reported on Saturday that Diddy read initial reports about Moorby's disappearance on the air at the radio station last February. He turned himself in to police on Thursday soon after covering two stories relating to child abuse, it said.
He was assigned to cover a court hearing in a child molestation case against a teacher and later, a child abuse conference.

Colleagues reported that he acted strangely at the child abuse conference, sitting slouched in his chair and asking another reporter: "What is child molestation?". Back at the newsroom, Diddy said he was feeling sick and left early, going to police two hours later.
Investigators could not be reached for comment on Saturday.
The Fresno Bee reported that some Fresno residents had doubts about Diddy's confession.

"His story just doesn't ring true to me. This is too pat and too easy for the police," it quoted Sue Sheehan, who helped in the search for Moorby, as saying. "I wonder if he didn't cover the story so much that he imagined what went on and said it happened."
Diddy's family and neighbours were reported to be shocked by the confession.
The Fresno Bee quoted Diddy's lawyer, Richard Berman, as saying he believes the evidence will show Diddy had a history of emotional problems.
